item.content:encoded:
Ukraine battles to keep lights on in Odesa as Russia strikes grid Reuters | Updated: 25-11-2026 17:50 IST | Created: 25-11-2026 17:50 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Inspecting the wreckage of a damaged electrical substation in Odesa, Dmytro Hryhoryev said the attack was part of Russian efforts to cut off the Black Sea port city — home to nearly 1 million people — from the rest of Ukraine. Odesa, Ukraine's largest port and the gateway for its grain exports to the rest of the world, has long been a target for Russian drone and missile attacks. But Hryhoryev, the local head of DTEK, Ukraine's largest private power company, said that Moscow has changed its tactics. Initially, Russia sought to destroy electricity generation capacity, but Ukraine has learned to restore that quickly, he said. So Moscow began attacking power transmission systems, like this substation. "The aim was to prevent the electricity still being generated in the country from being properly distributed between regions," Hryhoryev, 57, told Reuters, amid dangling wires and scattered chunks of concrete. DTEK chief executive Maxim Timchenko told Reuters this month that Ukraine was generating enough electricity to meet its needs but that the problem was delivering it from power stations in the western part of the country to consumers in other regions. Hryhoryev, the head of DTEK Odesa Power Grids, said Russia had attacked 60% of substations in the region but repairs had restored power supplies and infrastructure remained connected. "They (the Russians) continue to change tactics, attacking backbone networks in an attempt to prevent electricity from reaching our city altogether," he added, in reference to Ukraine's main power lines between regions. Russia denies deliberately targeting civilians during its war in Ukraine but says vital energy infrastructure is a legitimate target. Attacks on key components of the power-delivery system, which are often fitted with specialized, hard-to-replace equipment, can leave entire regions without electricity for days or even weeks. DTEK generates electricity at its five thermal power plants and distributes power to several regions, including Odesa, which does not have its own generation facilities. "We have substations that have been attacked three or four times. One substation was even attacked five times," Hryhoryev added. NEW ATTACKS Ukraine has repeatedly offered to halt its own attacks on Russia's oil refining facilities — which have damaged much of its production capacity — in return for Moscow suspending its strikes on electricity infrastructure. Russia has so far refused. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy says Moscow is striving to make Ukraine's major cities unliveable. Moscow launched a large-scale attack on Ukraine's energy system late last week, causing widespread power, heating and water supply outages in Odesa ahead of the winter plunge in temperatures. Two days after the attack, nearly 240,000 people remained without heating in wider Odesa, according to government data. "Unfortunately, we have learned to do things that are not described in any power engineering textbook. We do everything possible to return electricity more quickly," Hryhoryev said. "We have learned to work in rain and snow, to work at night, to work without breaks," he added. But Moscow has continued to attack Odesa and about 9,000 households in the region remained without power on Wednesday morning following an overnight strike. Russia again struck DTEK facilities, local authorities said.

item.title: Companies linked to Alice Huang raised financing against USD 301 million worth of AI equipment in China: Report
item.description: Companies linked to Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whose relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang triggered his brief resignation, raised financing against AI computing equipment valued at around ...
item.content:encoded:
Companies linked to Alice Huang raised financing against USD 301 million worth of AI equipment in China: Report Companies linked to Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whose relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang triggered his brief resignation, raised financing against AI computing equipment valued at around USD 301 million for major data centres in China, according to a Reuters report. ANI | Updated: 25-11-2026 16:27 IST | Created: 25-11-2026 16:27 IST

Representative image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Companies linked to Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whose relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang triggered his brief resignation, raised financing against AI computing equipment valued at around USD 301 million for major data centres in China, according to a Reuters report. Chinese central bank documents reviewed by Reuters identified up to 764 artificial intelligence (AI) servers and modules valued at USD 270 million, alongside networking equipment worth USD 31 million. Much of the hardware was listed at a major AI data centre in Shanghai. The records revealed that businesses linked to Alice Huang's family and associates helped finance and equip China's AI industry, even as US authorities investigated whether her Singapore-based company, Megaspeed, facilitated Chinese customers' access to restricted Nvidia technology. The financing arrangements highlight how Chinese technology companies are securing access to expensive AI computing infrastructure amid tightening US restrictions on advanced processors. On Monday, the US Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist. The company has denied wrongdoing and maintained that Alice Huang left the firm in August 2025. Alice Huang formerly controlled Megaspeed, a major overseas buyer of Nvidia processors. Her relationship with Jensen Huang, who resigned earlier this month before being reinstated 11 days later, has intensified scrutiny of Nvidia's business links with China. However, Reuters noted that the records do not establish whether the servers contained chips prohibited from being exported to China or how and when the equipment entered the country. Century Litong, an Nvidia preferred cloud partner, emerged as a key business involved in the financing arrangements. Financial records showed five leasing transactions covering up to 512 servers valued at around USD 200 million between May and December 2024. Four of the transactions listed equipment at the Yangtze River Delta AI supercomputing centre in Shanghai, a USD 6.3 billion complex developed by gaming company Century Huatong, in which Tencent holds a roughly 10 per cent stake. A Tencent spokesperson clarified that the company had never owned or operated the data centre project and that its investment in Century Huatong was focused on the gaming business. "Tencent has never entered into or otherwise had any commercial relationship with Megaspeed or any of its subsidiaries," the spokesperson said, as quoted by Reuters. Corporate records also linked Century Litong, Century Longteng and Century Huatong to Alice Huang's sister, Huang Yu, and her husband, investment executive Kang Wei. (ANI)

item.title: Pakistan military shelling in Balochistan's Mastung kills dozen, displaces 70,000
item.description: Pakistani military shelling and arson in Balochistan's Mastung district reportedly killed around a dozen people, injured hundreds, and affected 70,000 residents. Locals reported destroyed homes, ...
item.content:encoded:
Pakistan military shelling in Balochistan's Mastung kills dozen, displaces 70,000 Pakistani military shelling and arson in Balochistan's Mastung district reportedly killed around a dozen people, injured hundreds, and affected 70,000 residents. Locals reported destroyed homes, markets, and forced evictions. National Party leader Abdul Malik Baloch condemned the violence, calling for civilian protection, an end to forced displacement, and compensation. ANI | Updated: 25-11-2026 15:49 IST | Created: 25-11-2026 15:49 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Around a dozen people have reportedly been killed and hundreds injured in Pakistani military shelling in Balochistan's Mastung district, according to a report by The Balochistan Post (TBP), citing a delegation of residents who met National Party leader Abdul Malik Baloch. The delegation, comprising elders and representatives from Kardegap tehsil, informed Abdul Malik Baloch that approximately 70,000 people across four union councils had been affected by military operations. They also alleged that residents were being directed to leave their homes within 24 hours. According to the TBP report, the delegation said the burning of Killi Pasund Khan market in Gurgina had caused financial losses worth tens of millions of rupees. They reported the destruction of shops, livestock, dozens of houses and jewellery. The delegation further stated that all shops in Killi Guftari and Killi Khurasani had also been burned, while solar power systems serving agricultural schemes had been destroyed during the operations. The residents appealed to Abdul Malik Baloch to intervene to ensure the protection of local people and secure compensation for the losses suffered by affected families. According to TBP, Abdul Malik Baloch condemned the reported shelling, arson and intimidation by Pakistani forces, describing the reported burning of Killi Pasund Khan market as "deeply distressing and condemnable". He said protecting people's lives and property was a fundamental responsibility of the government. Abdul Malik Baloch also termed the removal of residents from their ancestral homes "unacceptable" and said the National Party rejected forced displacement. He further stated that civilians were facing "severe hardship, fear and insecurity", emphasising that the protection of human lives and fundamental rights must remain the priority in any action. The National Party leader reiterated that the safety and security of civilians must be ensured, while those affected by the reported military operations should receive protection and compensation for their losses. (ANI)
